title: Private networking onboarding & audit UX — PRD notes
content:
Context:
This doc is a product-first sketch for the private (VPC/on-prem) networking onboarding experience with an emphasis on: (1) making audit logs useful and discoverable for customers and auditors, (2) reducing friction in approval gates while preserving safety, and (3) clear handoff patterns for customer-managed networking. It’s intentionally UX-forward — we want to prototype flows that minimize back-and-forth with customer network teams and SREs.

Problem statement:
- Customers tell us onboarding a private deployment -> secure connectivity -> attestation and audit collection is the most painful part of procurement.
- Engineering support load spikes during first 30 days as we validate ACLs, peering, and certificate exchange.
- Existing audit telemetry is oriented toward operator teams; customers want a narrative (who did what, why) that maps to their compliance checklists.

Goals (success criteria):
- Customers can complete VPC/peering prescriptive checklist and submit the required artifacts with no more than one synchronous call to support in 80% of cases.
- Audit logs exposed to customers follow a standard schema and are queryable in-console; sample queries and export (CSV/JSON) available.
- Approval gates are automatable for common patterns (e.g., allowlist IPs, CIDR ranges, cert fingerprints) with manual override and an audit trail for all changes.

User journeys (high level):
1) Self-serve guided onboarding (recommended for small-mid customers):
   - Customer selects "Private (VPC)" in Console -> chooses new or existing VPC template.
   - Console shows a step-by-step network checklist with live validation (CIDR overlap check, reachable endpoint probe from our staging probe, TLS fingerprint validation).
   - Customer uploads proof artifacts (annotated diagram, firewall rules screenshot, peering request id).
   - Console runs automated validation agents where possible and provides exact list of outstanding items.

2) Assisted onboarding (large / regulated customers):
   - Customer requests a dedicated onboarding window.
   - We provision a temporary operator workspace that captures all handoff checkpoints and generates an immutable audit package (signed by both operator and customer admin).

Audit logs: schema & UX
- Core fields (minimal): timestamp, actor-id (email/service-account), action, target-resource, before, after, reason (free text), artifact-refs (list), request-id.
- Structured context: network-change-type (peering/open-port/route-add), customer-assertion (boolean), approval-flow-id.
- Customer-facing UX:
   - Timeline view grouped by day and type with quick filters (network, keys, approvals).
   - A "forensics export" button to produce a tiled report (log + artifacts + validation results) suitable for audit teams.
   - Retention & export controls: customers can request extended retention (enterprise add-on) and schedule daily exports to customer S3 or syslog endpoint.

Approval gates design (principles):
- Default to "allow automation for low-risk changes": e.g., adding an allowlist IP that matches an existing CIDR block -> auto-approve with email notification.
- High-risk changes (route deletes, BGP peering modifications, IAM role grants) require explicit approver(s) and must be bound to a policy.
- Multi-stage approvals: support 1) automated validation, 2) technical approver sign-off, 3) legal/contractual sign-off for cross-org connectivity.
- All approvals generate an immutable record and are surfaced in the audit timeline.

Operator & customer handoff artifacts:
- Required minimal artifact set for onboarding: network diagram (PNG/PDF), CIDR list, firewall rules export, peering request id, x509 cert fingerprint, contact list with ssh-jump endpoints.
- Optional: packet-capture sample, traceroute log, policy-as-code snippet (terraform snippet showing route/policy).
- Storage: artifacts attached to the approval-flow-id and hashed into the immutable audit record (hash stored in logs).

Telemetry & observability expectations:
- Key metrics: time-to-onboard, number of validation cycles, number of manual interventions, support tickets opened per onboarding.
- Error taxonomy for onboarding failures (validation-failed, network-probe-timeout, certificate-mismatch, permission-denied).
- Alerts: product should emit alerts to our SRE when onboarding stalls > 48h for high-value customers.

Privacy & compliance notes:
- Artifacts may contain PII — ensure artifact storage complies with customer retention policy and encryption @ rest/in transit.
- We must provide the ability to redact sensitive fields in exported audit packages on customer request.

Edge / failure scenarios to handle:
- Customer changes network mid-onboarding (CIDR reassign) -> require a re-validation gating step and mark previous approvals as stale.
- Customer-managed firewall silently blocks validation probes -> provide clear remediation steps and an "I want a test-box" mode where customers can request a short-lived external test endpoint.
- Rollback: approval flows should include an explicit rollback artifact and a playbook (who to notify, how to revert routes/config).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How opinionated should the console checkers be? (E.g., should we enforce specific ciphers? This reduces support but may block some customers.)
- Export formats: add Excel templates for enterprise auditors or keep to JSON/CSV only?
- Do we sign audit packages with our platform key or provide a customer-verified signing flow?

Proposed next steps (short-term roadmap):
- Week 1–2: workshop with solutions engineering + SRE to finalize artifact list and probe design. (Owner: Daniel)
- Week 3–6: prototype console checklist with live validation and a mock timeline view. (Owner: Maya)
- Week 7–10: build audit export and attach-hash pipeline, basic retention toggle in console. (Owner: Product infra squad)
- Parallel: define approval-gate policy DSL (RFC) for common network operations and map to Jira tickets.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conversational — want feedback on:
  - minimal artifact set (are we asking for too much?)
  - acceptable automation boundaries for approvals
  - UX for audit timeline and export requirements
